title: Deep learning finds an ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death
summary: A deep learning model trained on about 440,000 Swedish ECGs linked to death certificates isolates a high-risk group (2.2% of the sample) with a 7.0% annual sudden cardiac death rate, versus 4.6% for reduced LVEF; 86.1% of its high-risk patients were not flagged by LVEF. It was externally validated in a US health system and a Taiwanese registry. The press release reports a 54.4% lower-than-expected mortality among high-risk patients with implanted defibrillators, read as a benefit; the paper was published in Nature with the press release dated 2026-11-12 (Europe PMC first-online date 2026-06-24).
ai_technology: Deep learning ECG model with a generative ECG waveform model for visualization
organization: UC Berkeley; Swedish region health data; US health system; Taiwanese hospital registry

evidence.tested: Model trained on Swedish ECG-death linkage data, then evaluated in a US health system and a Taiwanese hospital registry for arrhythmic cardiac arrest prediction.
evidence.unknown: Mortality benefit of defibrillators is an observational association, not a randomized result (press release framing). Not stated in the reviewed material for other limits.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model discovered the predictive ECG waveform pattern; generative model used to visualize it.
